key_insight: APOE effects on disease risk and plasma proteins vary by ancestry and sex, with some signals strongest in neurological and lipid-related traits and a few potentially portable biomarkers emerging across groups.
clinical_relevance: These findings support ancestry-aware interpretation of APOE-based risk and may help refine how APOE status is used to understand Alzheimer’s, liver, and cardiometabolic risk.
method: Phenome-wide association study of APOE genotypes in 367,757 All of Us participants across six ancestry groups.
Tested APOE alleles against 2,632 phenotypes using an ordered Alzheimer’s-risk genotype hierarchy with covariate adjustment.
Analyzed plasma protein associations for APOE ε2 and ε4 dosage in 9,132 participants across five ancestries.
evidence_signal: The study identified 27 APOE-associated phenotypes, including sex-heterogeneous lipid traits, ancestry-specific liver and dementia effects, and proteomic links such as SNAP25 across ancestries.
watch_item: Because several associations differed by ancestry and sex, results may not transfer cleanly across populations without local validation and replication.
paper_title: Phenome-wide and proteomic analysis of APOE alleles across different ancestries in the All of Us Research Program
